name: Real-time efficiency and deployment
gist: Papers making vision-language and robot policies fast enough to run on real robots in real time, using techniques like token pruning, model compression, and efficient inference.
explain: Modern robot policies are often built from large neural networks trained on internet-scale data. A model might have hundreds of millions of adjustable internal weights—the values that the network uses to make predictions. Running this model on a real robot is a problem. The robot has onboard compute—a small GPU or CPU, not a data center. A large model might take five seconds to produce an action, but the robot needs to react in 100 milliseconds. Also, the model might not fit in memory. And if it takes too much power to run, the robot's battery runs out in an hour instead of a day. So the challenge is: how do you keep the intelligence and capability of large models while making them fast and small enough to run on a robot?

The difficulty is that scaling down a model usually means losing capability. If you shrink the network, remove layers, or quantize weights (represent them with fewer bits), the model becomes faster because it does less computation, but less accurate because it has fewer internal adjustable values to store the patterns it learned. Where is the sweet spot? Also, different robots have different compute budgets. A research robot in a lab might have a high-end GPU. A delivery robot has a small embedded processor. A surgical robot needs absolute reliability and cannot retrain in the field. So efficiency is not a one-size-fits-all problem. It depends on the robot, the task, and the environment.

Papers address this through model compression—techniques to make models smaller and faster without losing too much accuracy, because smaller models have fewer parameters to compute and fewer values to move through memory. Some prune tokens: instead of processing every detail in the image, the model learns which parts of the image are important for the task and skips processing the others, saving computation. Some use distillation: train a small model to imitate a large one. Some quantize weights or use mixed precision—use fewer bits for some weights and normal precision for others. Others optimize the model for specific hardware, rewriting the model to use the instruction set and memory layout of a specific GPU, which makes it faster on that particular hardware because the memory access patterns match the hardware design. The central insight is that real deployment requires thinking about compute from the start, not as an afterthought.

papers.title: BOLT: Decision‑Aligned Distillation and Budget-Aware Routing for Constrained Multimodal QA on Robots
papers.contribution: Robo2VLM-1 student distilled from LLaVA-1.5-13B improves accuracy from 28.66 to 50.50 with lower calibration error and 89% memory reduction (26,878 to 3,035 MB).

papers.title: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Models across XPUs: Constraints and Acceleration for On-Robot Deployment
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 2.9x speedup on GPUs and 6x on edge NPUs with only marginal degradation, showing edge devices can be more efficient than flagship GPUs.

papers.title: SP-VLA: A Joint Model Scheduling and Token Pruning Approach for VLA Model Acceleration
papers.contribution: Reduces temporal and spatial redundancy in VLA models, achieving effective acceleration while maintaining focus on critical actions and salient visual information.

papers.title: When a Robot is More Capable than a Human: Learning from Constrained Demonstrators
papers.contribution: Outperforms behavioral cloning in sample efficiency and task completion; on WidowX arm, achieves 11-second task completion, 10x faster than behavioral cloning.

papers.title: Efficient Differentiable Contact Model with Long-range Influence
papers.contribution: Enables discovery of complex contact-rich control signals from simple initializations for locomotion and manipulation tasks.

papers.title: FastVGGT: Fast Visual Geometry Transformer
papers.contribution: Achieves 4x speedup on 1000-image sequences while mitigating error accumulation without retraining.

papers.title: Learning High-Frequency Continuous Action Chunks in Latent Space
papers.contribution: Enables robots to execute complex contact-rich tasks continuously with less pauses and jerky motions compared to action-space baselines.

papers.title: Rethinking Instruction Drift as a Sampling Error: SNR-Aware Power Distributions for Long-Horizon Robotic Planning
papers.contribution: CAPS achieves substantial improvements over strong baselines without parameter updates on RoboTwin, Simpler-WindowX, and Libero-long benchmarks.
